facts.raw_span: A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
intermittent generalized pruritus
blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa
no granulomas or malignant cells were identified
A 36-year-old man with no prior medical history presented with a 4-year history of diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
intermittent generalized pruritus
blurred vision, bilateral exophthalmos, and difficulty walking
mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate: mildly elevated
bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes of the distal femora and proximal tibiae
intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri
bilateral symmetric uptake in long bones, right clavicle, and mandible, with uptake in subcutaneous and muscle tissues of the lower limbs
enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues
diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis with rare Touton-like giant cells
Immunohistochemical staining of the histiocytes was positive for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa
no granulomas or malignant cells were identified

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, sclerotic changes, and histiocytic infiltration with foamy histiocytes and Touton-like giant cells is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease, a rare histiocytic disorder.

Although the patient's histiocytes were negative for CD1a, S100, and langerin, the presence of foamy histiocytes and Touton-like giant cells could suggest Langerhans cell histiocytosis, but the lack of specific markers and the clinical presentation make Erdheim-Chester disease more likely.

The patient's skeletal findings, including sclerotic changes and uptake on bone scintigraphy, could be consistent with skeletal sarcoidosis, but the presence of histiocytic infiltration and the lack of granulomas make this diagnosis less likely.

This diagnosis is considered due to the multifocal nature of the patient's skeletal findings and the presence of histiocytic infiltration, but Erdheim-Chester disease is a more comprehensive diagnosis that explains the patient's systemic symptoms and histiocytic findings.

rationales.F07: Intramedullary sclerosis is a feature of Erdheim-Chester disease

rationales.F09: Pituitary and retrobulbar lesions are highly suggestive of Erdheim-Chester disease

rationales.F11: Immunohistochemical staining pattern is consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease
